summary.headline: Paramount Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore; operating margin (ex other income) expanded 320 bps YoY to 6.6%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 17.4% YoY to INR 529.4 crore but fell 7.7% QoQ, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4-to-Q1 pattern. Operating profit excluding other income rose 129.2% YoY to INR 34.7 crore, with margin up 320 bps YoY and 136 bps QoQ to 6.6%. The US export recovery after the IEEPA tariff invalidation drove exports to INR 155 crore (29%+ of revenue, up about 77% QoQ), while domestic revenue reached INR 374 crore. Order book rose to INR 615 crore from INR 583 crore, and a fresh equity raise of about INR 122 crore lifted net worth to INR 894 crore.

segments.name: Power cables
segments.commentary: Accounted for 57.2% of Q1 revenue; power cable order book INR 455 crore (about 74% of total orders), up 27% YoY.

segments.name: Domestic B2B industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 296 crore, up 92% YoY; management cites this higher-margin institutional mix as a margin driver.

segments.name: Exports (US-led)
segments.commentary: INR 155 crore in Q1, 29%+ of revenue; US distributors grew from 2 in FY22 to 8 now. Export order book only INR 97 crore.

segments.name: HTLS conductors
segments.commentary: Management cites INR 100 crore of business in hand; capacity build-out expected to be margin-accretive.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, constrained by existing plants running at effectively 100% utilisation.
EBITDA margin expected to return to FY25 levels (about 8% pre-tariff, per analyst framing) by Q4 FY27; operating margin of 6.6% is 'on track'.
FY27 US exports targeted at INR 700-800 crore, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.
Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; ~INR 500 crore revenue expected in FY28 and INR 1,200 crore by FY29 at 75% utilisation.
Long-term target of INR 5,000 crore revenue by FY31; management hopes to exceed it.
Working capital cycle to be kept within 90-100 days.
Debt-equity to stay below 0.3x after Narmadapuram phase 1, with a term loan planned later.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) is the third plant; phase 1 capex about INR 300 crore; about INR 30 crore+ spent so far; most critical machinery ordered; civil construction mobilised with 6-7 months expected for major works.
INR 65 crore of the equity raise earmarked for Narmadapuram; no debt drawn yet as of Q1.
Over the past 3-4 years, more than INR 155 crore spent on existing plants (Dharuhera, Khushkhera).

Approved up to 66 kV; 132 kV approvals expected to start within about a year of manufacturing start (one or two possibly in 6-8 months), with all approvals targeted by FY29. E-beam cables are a new product, with major certifications targeted by end-FY29.
Management is evaluating 220 kV and 400 kV products; not officially guided.
demand_pricing: Management describes demand as broad-based across power grid, renewables, data centres, railways/metro and construction; order inflows are firmer than anticipated at the start of the year.
US tariff regime normalised after the US Supreme Court invalidated IEEPA tariffs; management says India is now at par with other exporters.
Export order book is kept deliberately low (INR 97 crore) because firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery and most customers now bear tariff changes.
Key US competitors are South Korea, Vietnam and Cambodia, with Egypt, Ecuador and Turkey emerging. Management says the company faced 25%+ duty last year versus 10-18% for rivals.
Metal throughput up about 4% YoY (absolute figure not disclosed; last year's base cited as roughly 29,000 tons).
New US product: solar cables above 600 V; exports have started, with margins expected similar to current levels.
Existing plants are at effectively 100% utilisation; management says the constraint is manufacturing capacity, not demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to pre-tariff levels near 8%, and what drove the 320 bps YoY margin improvement and can it be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is in line with expectations and FY25-level margins are targeted by at least Q4 FY27. Drivers cited: normalisation of US exports after the IEEPA duties were struck down (expected to add 300+ bps), and a higher-margin domestic power cable mix (~57% of Q1 revenue). Exports were 29%+ of revenue vs 15% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Narmadapuram, and are there cost or time overruns?
qa_highlights.answer: Most critical machinery is ordered, with delivery lead times long but expected on time. Civil construction has started and major works are expected to take 6-7 months. Management does not expect major overruns. About INR 30 crore+ has been spent, plus more than INR 155 crore over three to four years on existing plants.

qa_highlights.question: How is Narmadapuram capex funded, and what utilisation supports the INR 1,200 crore revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No debt drawn yet; funding is from equity raised, internal accruals and planned term loan. Post phase 1, debt-equity is targeted below 0.3x. INR 1,200 crore is at 75% utilisation (the CFO-level comment referred to FY29). Approvals up to 66 kV are in place; 132 kV approvals are expected to start within about a year of manufacturing, with some possibly in 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the export order book only INR 97 crore despite strong export revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is deliberately keeping export orders low: firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months delivery, and most customers now bear tariff changes. Management still expects INR 700-800 crore of US exports this year, versus INR 155 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is current capacity utilisation, and what growth is possible in FY27 versus FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing plants run at practically 100% utilisation, and the constraint is manufacturing capacity rather than demand. FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%. FY28 growth is expected to be much faster once Narmadapuram starts. The INR 5,000 crore FY31 target is seen as a floor to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin progress at risk if H2 export mix falls, and how do export margins compare with domestic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export EBITDA was negative in FY26, about -4% to -4.5% at EBITDA level. Pre-FY26 export margins were about 1.5% above domestic. It said the company can pivot quickly between domestic and export, citing FY23 and FY25 shifts, and expects export margins to keep improving each quarter.

risks_watch: Narmadapuram execution: long machinery lead times, 6-7 month civil works, and a phase 1 capex of about INR 300 crore against INR 30 crore+ spent so far.
US tariff regime durability and export recovery: the target of INR 700-800 crore of exports versus a low export order book of INR 97 crore.
Margin path to FY25 levels (about 8% EBITDA) by Q4 FY27 from 6.6% operating margin; watch whether H2 export mix dilutes margins.
132 kV and EHV approvals timing (first approvals possibly 6-8 months after manufacturing starts; all by FY29) and E-beam certifications targeted by end-FY29.
Working capital: cash conversion cycle at 96 days versus the 90-100 day target; receivable days fell to 64 from 79.

Metal price and aluminium exposure: management says firm-price orders are capped at 3-4 months, but variable-price and +/- pass-through still carry some variation risk. Metal throughput was only disclosed as up about 4% YoY.
key_quotes: We delivered one of our strongest quarters on record, with healthy improvement across revenue, EBITDA, and profitability.

The 6.6% operating margin which excludes other income is quite a meaningful step for us to achieve the FY25 levels that we hope to close with in the current financial year, by atleast the last quarter of FY27.
Because, for Paramount the problem in is not selling, the problem is manufacturing, because our capacity has been constrained.
We do not expect to cross the level of 0.3x at best by the time we complete the first phase of our Narmadapuram project.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the quarter, margins and US recovery, but cautious on export order visibility and on the pace of EHV approvals. Management was evasive on absolute metal throughput and on the exact debt split for Narmadapuram.
